requirement:
When authoring evidence for a named example, its complete fenced declaration
MUST be included in the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.examples.authoring_inputs` has one operative clause: "When authoring evidence for a named example, its complete fenced declaration MUST be included in the mandatory input set defined by `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`." That clause is about observable behavior: which content ends up in the set of inputs supplied to an assessment. It doesn't name a library, algorithm, signature, type, field or interface that must be used.

I checked whether any part of the clause is a structural obligation by imagining a different implementation. Suppose the harness collects the example's declaration through a different internal path, such as a different function, struct or lookup mechanism. The mandatory input set would still contain the whole fenced declaration, and the clause would still be satisfied. The way the harness builds the set is therefore up to the implementation.

The cited `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` is context only. It defines the contribution, deduplication and reporting rules, and it is not the subject here. Its own obligations are assessed against its own text.

There are no implementation roots and no acknowledgments. Since every clause is behavioral, no implementation evidence is needed for this requirement, and I found no gap.

behavioral: The only obligation is that, when authoring evidence for a named example, the example's complete fenced declaration is in the mandatory input set.

- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]` creates `:::{example} case` with a body that contains cite and test roles. It calls `AssessmentSources::prepare(..., "requirements.case")` and checks that `subject_kind` is the Example definition kind. It asserts that `mandatory_inputs()[0]["requirements"]` is `requirements.case`. It also asserts that `mandatory_inputs()[0]["text"]` equals the exact full list of lines: the opening fence `:::{example} case`, the body line, and the closing `:::`. That assertion enforces that the whole fenced declaration is present, including both fences.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_metadata_is_hidden_in_fenced_sections_and_preserved_in_details]` covers the `:::{example} case` variant, which has multi-line citation metadata. For `guide.case` it asserts that `sources.subject_text` contains the full citation text. It also asserts that some mandatory input's joined text contains that citation text. So the declaration is not truncated or stripped of its citation lines in the input set.

Together these tests check inclusion and completeness of the example declaration. A harness that omitted the example, or included only its body or only part of its lines, would fail them. I found no further distinctions in the requirement text. Deduplication and the other input contributions belong to `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, which is cited context and not reassessed here.
